stories.text: Ahmed Abdallah Bishr, the general chief of staff for the Gathering of Sudan Liberation Forces (GSLF), dies of the wounds he suffered a month ago during an assassination attack by drone strike against his home in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan.
The Iranian military attacks, with drones and missiles, an American military facility in Bahrain, in one of the largest attacks on the country in months.
The Philippines, with the song "Sobra-Sobra" by Carmelle, wins the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia held in Bangkok, Thailand.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association threatens to indefinitely close unrest-affected factories without pay under the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006, after ongoing wage protests force the shutdown of 55 units and halt production at 147 others.

stories.topic: Canada–Philippines relations, Free trade agreements of Canada
stories.text: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney announces that negotiations for a free-trade agreement (FTA) with the Philippines have concluded, with signing expected in 2027. The FTA would eliminate more than 90% of tariff lines.
A bus overturns on the Garzón–Neiva highway in Colombia, killing six people and wounding eleven more.
Four workers are killed after a methane gas explosion at a mine in Chita, Boyacá Department, Colombia.
The Slagdijkstermolen windmill in Friesland, Netherlands, burns down.
Eight more people in Bangladesh are reported to have died from dengue fever, bringing this year's outbreak's death toll to 491.
Border Guard Bangladesh seize 48 high-power explosive gel sticks, 100 detonators, and 11 fuses during an operation along the Bangladesh–India border in Kanaighat Upazila, Sylhet District, Bangladesh.
The Guatemalan Army begins deploying a battalion to the departments of Zacapa, Izabal, and Chiquimula following an attack in the Zacapa Department the previous day that killed five people.
Student protesters, unions, and the yellow vests hold another nationwide protest in France, with over 100,000 participants.

The South Sudanese election commission postpones the country's first presidential and parliamentary elections since independence in 2011 from December 22, 2026, to February 11, 2027, amid political tensions and continuing violence.

The Italian Data Protection Authority fines American technology company Meta for €805 million (US$887 million) after it was found that the Facebook Android app had access to users' photos and videos without specific consent or disclosure.
